title: A push delivers the orchestrator's whole HEAD, and nothing can withhold a path from a member
foundBy: feature request from another agent, relayed by the user (host); the clone probe below is this session's
details:
`cs-campaign-member push <agent> [repo]` sends the orchestrator's HEAD to the member at `refs/campaign/orchestrator`. The orchestrator cannot name another commit. A push carries the commit's whole history, so every path on that line arrives in the member's clone whether or not the member merges it.

A campaign can be designed so that one member must never see certain files the orchestrator holds, such as a directory of expected results. One push from the wrong checkout delivers them with the history. Nothing refuses it, nothing records it, and a corrective push to an earlier commit is refused as non-fast-forward. Such a campaign can only find a breach afterwards, by scanning clones, and the log gives it nothing to scan.

The push is not the only route. A member's repository is a full bare clone of the host repository, every branch included, and the profile's `ref` picks the checkout rather than the history. A withheld path that exists on any branch of the host repository is therefore in every member's clone at create. The clone is also made from a local path, which copies the object store as it stands. A probe on git 2.53 showed the difference: a blob dropped by `git reset --hard`, reachable only from the reflog, was present in a `git clone --bare <path>` and absent from a `git clone --bare file://<path>`. A ref walk cannot see such an object.

What would help, in order:

- A `withhold` list on a member's repository and snapshot entries. `validate` and `create` hold it against every object reachable from every ref of the host repository, and refuse a host repository that holds objects no ref reaches.
- A push that refuses when any object it would newly deliver sits at a withheld path, judged against the refs the member already holds.
- A log entry for every delivery and every refusal, naming the member, the repository, the commit and the outcome.
- A `--commit` flag, so a push can name what it sends.

The fence covers the git channel only. The text of every `send` is already in the archive, and the tool cannot stop a model from pasting a file into a dispatch.
